name: Hyperion DB
target_user: Embedded systems engineers and database architects
problem: Embedded transactional data stores struggle with maintaining strict ACID guarantees under power failure without incurring massive synchronous disk write overheads.
pain: Standard embedded stores either sacrifice atomicity and durability or rely on monolithic engines that consume excessive memory and lack deterministic recovery paths.
solution: A robust C11 storage engine implementing write-ahead logging with fuzzy checkpoints, page-level latching, lock management with deadlock detection, and a Volcano-style execution model.
verification: Deterministic integration suite testing crash recovery across simulated abrupt process termination, transaction rollback on constraint violations, and concurrent thread stress testing under memory pressure.
major_features: ARIES-style recovery subsystem managing write-ahead logging, analysis, redo, and undo phases
Buffer pool manager implementing a clock-sweep page replacement algorithm with frame pinning
B+Tree on-disk index manager supporting concurrent node splitting, merging, and leaf node lookups
Lock manager featuring granular table, page, and tuple locks with wait-for graph deadlock detection
Custom SQL lexer, recursive-descent parser, and relational algebra AST generator
Cost-based query optimizer utilizing table statistics and index histograms for join ordering
Volcano-style physical execution engine supporting nested-loop joins, sequential scans, and projections
Crash-recovery verification harness injecting simulated power failures during active write transactions
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
